question: The philosophical concept that everything in the universe is one divine essence is called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahman** is a key concept in Hindu philosophy, representing the ultimate reality or the divine essence that permeates everything in the universe.
 
• It is described as the eternal, unchanging, infinite, and formless reality, which is the source and foundation of all existence.
 
• In the **Upanishads**, Brahman is often discussed as the ultimate truth that transcends the physical world and is beyond human comprehension.
 
• The concept of Brahman is closely connected to the idea of **Atman**, which refers to the individual soul. Hindu philosophy often emphasizes the unity of Atman and Brahman, signifying the connection between the self and the universal reality.
 
• This philosophical idea is a central theme in **Advaita Vedanta**, a prominent school of Hindu philosophy, which teaches that there is no distinction between Brahman and Atman.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Samiti:**

 
 
• Samiti is a term used in ancient Indian history to refer to an assembly or gathering, often for decision-making purposes.
 
• It is not related to the philosophical concept of divine essence but is significant in the context of governance and social organization in ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Yajna:**
 
 
• Yajna refers to a ritual sacrifice performed in Vedic traditions, involving offerings made to deities through fire.
 
• It symbolizes the idea of reciprocity between humans and the divine but does not represent the concept of the universe being one divine essence.
 
 
 
• **Purandar:**
 
 
• Purandar is a name associated with the Hindu deity Indra, the king of gods in Vedic mythology.
 
• It does not align with the philosophical idea of Brahman, which signifies a universal divine essence rather than a specific deity.
 
 
 
• **Brahman:**
 
 
• The concept of Brahman is foundational in Hinduism and is discussed extensively in sacred texts such as the **Upanishads** and the **Bhagavad Gita**.
 
• It is often described as the supreme cosmic spirit or consciousness that is both immanent and transcendent.
 
• Philosophical schools like **Advaita Vedanta** interpret Brahman as non-dual, suggesting that the ultimate reality is undivided and singular.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Upanishads:**

 
 
• These ancient texts are philosophical treatises that explore the nature of reality, self, and the universe.
 
• The concept of Brahman is central in these texts, often described as the ultimate truth and reality.
 
 
 
• **Advaita Vedanta:**
 
 
• This school of philosophy advocates the non-duality of Brahman and Atman, asserting that there is no distinction between the individual soul and the universal essence.
 
• It was profoundly developed by **Adi Shankaracharya**, a key figure in Indian philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Vedic Texts:**
 
 
• While the early Vedic texts primarily focus on rituals and deities, the later texts like Upanishads delve deeper into metaphysical concepts such as Brahman.
 
• These texts form the basis of much of Hindu philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The understanding of Brahman influences not only religious practices but also philosophical inquiries into the nature of existence, consciousness, and the universe.
 
• It serves as a unifying principle in Hindu thought, connecting diverse beliefs and practices.
